# v1.1.0-dev.64 — Every virtual display, not just Parsec

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.63`.

WLM was built against Parsec's virtual display and it showed. The
display feature could recognise exactly one driver. Everything it
said was worded as though no other kind existed.

## It Knows What Kind Of Display It Is Looking At

Every virtual display on Windows is built on the same Microsoft
driver model. They all behave the same awkward way: the display's
hardware path changes every time it's created, the resolution list
changes while the app is watching, the scaling control sometimes
reports nonsense, and Windows will happily say a resolution change
worked when nothing moved.

WLM already coped with all four. It just called them Parsec.

Now it recognises the driver behind a display and says so.
Parsec, Apollo's SudoVDA, the community Virtual Display Driver and
the IddSampleDriver builds it grew out of, USB Mobile Monitor,
spacedesk, Citrix, Remote Desktop, and the graphics adapters in
Hyper-V, VirtualBox and VMware. A display from a driver WLM has
never heard of is still recognised as virtual rather than mistaken
for a monitor on your desk.

Your displays read **Left 1440p · Parsec virtual** now, or whichever
driver it actually is.

## Adding A Resolution Says Who Can Do It

The **Add resolutions** button used to promise the same thing for
every display. It couldn't deliver it, because only Parsec publishes
a way for another app to add a resolution to its driver.

So that's the only place WLM offers to do it. For anything else the
window tells you who can:

```
spacedesk resolutions                              read-only

spacedesk takes its resolution from the client device.
Change it in the spacedesk viewer, then reconnect.
```

The alternative was guessing. The community driver keeps its
resolutions in a file that moved between two names across releases.
Picking the wrong one means writing into somebody else's driver
config. Being told where to go beats a button that quietly does
nothing.

The same applies when a resolution won't apply. The warning names
your driver and what to do about it. A physical monitor no longer
gets a virtual-display explanation for a problem that isn't one.

## Smaller Things

- The slot counter follows what you're editing. Adding a row used to
  leave "0 of 2 yours" on screen next to a row you could plainly see.
- Parsec's own reserved slots are labelled per row and explained once,
  instead of one sentence doing both jobs badly.

## Under The Hood

Working out what a display is now happens in one place. It used to
happen in three. Those three had already disagreed twice, each time
filing a display's settings under an identity that doesn't survive a
reconnect. A fourth copy went in during this change and
told a spacedesk display that WLM didn't know how to help it, while
the right answer sat two files away. That copy is gone.

Nothing about your profiles or rules changes. Settings written
before this still resolve.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
